is filed by the appellants claiming for enhancement of compensation and MFA No.7227/2023 is filed by the Managing Director, KSRTC disputing the liability.

2. Both the appeals are filed against the award dated 13.03.2023 passed in MVC No.1194/2021 by the Court of III Additional District and Sessions Judge, AMACT, Tumakuru, (for short 'Tribunal').
3.

sentences.text:
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their rank and status before the Tribunal.
4.
Heard the arguments of both counsel appearing in both the appeals.
5. Brief facts of the case are that, Sri. Suresh K, met with an accident on 21.09.2021.

His NC:
2026:KHC:13687 HC-KAR sisters and brother filed claim application claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.

The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted Rs.21,81,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
Aggrieved by the said order, the claimants have filed appeal in MFA No.1991/2024 for enhancement of compensation.
6. It is contended that Suresh K was working as Head Cook in Nanjundeshwara Hotel and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to his untimely death, the petitioners have suffered loss of dependency and affection.
But the Tribunal has considered the income of the appellant at Rs.15,000/- which is on the lower side.
Further, it is contended that the claimants are Class-II legal heirs of deceased K Suresh and also they are major.

But according to Motor Vehicles Act, the legal heirs of the deceased is entitled for the compensation as per the decisions rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation, NC: 2026:KHC:13687 HC-KAR Ahmedabad vs.

Prabhatbhai and Another1

and in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Birender and Ors, and also decision rendered in the case of Managing Director, KSRTC vs.
Venkataramanappa K S and others 2.

Birender and Ors

sentences.text: Therefore, the appellants have requested for enhancement of compensation.

7. On contrary against the very same judgment, the Managing Director, KSRTC has filed appeal in MFA No.7227/2023 and mainly contended that the Tribunal is justified in taking the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- in the absence of any income proof.

Claimant Nos.1 and 2 are married sisters of deceased and they are residing at Mysuru and Maruvanahalli village ie., in their matrimonial homes and claimant No.3 is residing in Bidadi but the deceased was staying separately in Tumakuru.

As such, the claimants are not entitled for compensation reported in (1987) 3 Supreme Court Cases 234 reported in 2003 ACJ 597 NC: 2026:KHC:13687 HC-KAR under the head Managing Director Ksrtc vs Bhagya on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124850948/
4 'loss of dependency' but they are entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of estate'.

8. Further, the learned counsel relied upon the judgment rendered by this Court in the case of A.
Manavalagan vs. A.Krishnamurthy and Others3 wherein it is specifically stated that though the quantum of savings will vary from person to person, there is a need to standardise the quantum of savings for determining the loss to estate in the absence of specific evidence to the contrary and the savings can be taken as 15% of the income.

entities.text:
A.
Manavalagan vs. A.Krishnamurthy and Others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case on hand, the claimant Nos.1 and 2 are married sisters and claimant No.3 is the brother who is employed and not dependant on his brother who died in the accident and the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the deceased as savings and award the amount as specified in Manavalagan's case stated supra.
Further, the Tribunal has granted reported in ILR 2004 KAR 3268 NC: 2026:KHC:13687 HC-KAR compensation under the heads loss of consortium to which the claimants are not entitled as discussed above.

9. Further, the learned counsel for respondent relied upon the judgment dated 17.10.2025 of this Court passed in MFA No.3886/2020 c/w. MFA No.4216/2020 in the case of the National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. George Menezes and Others, wherein it is held that in the absence of cogent positive evidence to assess the monthly income of the deceased, considering the date of accident, age and occupation of the deceased, the monthly income can be notionally determined.
10.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. George Menezes and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Lastly, learned counsel contended that the Tribunal has not deducted the interim compensation of Rs.25,000/- which was paid by them on humanitarian ground which is ought to have deducted from the total compensation but the same is not done by the Tribunal.
11. Suresh was aged 32 years and appropriate multiplier is to be taken as '16'.

Though the appellants NC: 2026:KHC:13687 HC-KAR have stated that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month,
they have not filed single document to prove his income and the accident occurred on 21.09.2021,
the notional income of Rs.15,000/- was confirmed as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the same.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others4,
40% is to be added towards future prospectus and as per the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation5, 50% is to be deducted towards personal expenses since the deceased is a bachelor.

Apart from that, the appellants are also entitled for Rs.33,000/- towards 'conventional heads' as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC:13687 HC-KAR Limited Vs.
